content:
The inaugural AARO TechX Summit is underway this week through September 26th at the Hilton Garden Inn in Mississauga, Ont., bringing automotive repair professionals together for three days of advanced technical training, focused on the rapidly changing demands of modern vehicle repair.

With technical education spanning conventional powertrains, emerging vehicle technology and advanced diagnostics, AARO TechX represents a significant new training initiative for Canada’s independent repair sector. Hosted by the Automotive Aftermarket Repair Organization of Canada (AARO), the summit is designed to give independent repair facilities practical, high-level training they can take directly back to the shop.

Day One features a mix of sessions covering diagnostics, emissions, communications, diesel technology and shop-level diagnostic strategy. Each day offers two separate tracks (seminar options) for different skill focuses.

Among the featured Day One tracks is “A Match Made with Combustion,” presented by David Finch, an experienced shop operations manager with a demonstrated history of diesel technical support and training. The session examined modern diesel emissions and induction systems, including emissions treatment, system design and fuel-economy considerations. The session also features a closer look at Duramax L5P, 6.7L Powerstroke and 3.0L Duramax platforms.

Connected-vehicle technology is another major focus, with instructor Ju Chen, a diagnostics expert and a board member at AARO, presenting “RF Communication.” The session explored the growing role of wireless communication systems in vehicles, including key fobs, keyless entry, TPMS, navigation and cellular systems, as well as wireless diagnostics and troubleshooting.

For technicians looking to build further diagnostic expertise, Leroy Martin’s “Building a Profitable Diagnostic Specialist Career” addressed diagnostic case studies, unconventional testing approaches and strategies for documenting and communicating the testing process with a business-building lens.

The summit will continue through Saturday the 26th, with Day Two having an EV system and electrical testing and equipment focus. Day Three will feature advanced network and scan tool diagnostics.

Stay tuned for further highlights and recap on AARO’s inaugural TechX training summit.

About AARO Canada

The Automotive Aftermarket Repair Organization of Canada (AARO) is an action-oriented, not-for profit association dedicated to representing, supporting and strengthening Canada’s independent  automotive service and repair industry. AARO provides its members with advocacy, education and  training, industry information, business resources, networking opportunities and programs  designed to help independent repair businesses succeed in a rapidly changing automotive industry. aaro.ca
